notes:
- Background: SignalFrame builds a realtime code assistant embedded in their IDE plugin (Electron + native ext). Primary goal is indistinguishable latency vs local completions.
- Key ask: low-latency streaming + token-budget controls to keep predictive typing snappy and avoid mid-sentence stalls. TTFT target: 30-80ms for cold completions, steady-state token stream <= 15ms jitter.
- Engineering quote: "If the user types and there's any perceivable lag we lose flow — need TTFT <= 50ms typical, with graceful degradation."
- Technical constraints: editor sends very small prompt deltas (last 64 tokens); need incremental KV reuse, minimal re-tokenization. Must support WebSocket and SSE fallback for corporate proxies.
- Token budgeting: session budget ~120-150 tokens per completion request by default; want dynamic refill based on idle time and cursor movement. Need tooling to tune per-workflow (refactor vs generate).
- Backpressure plan: enforce soft-stop at 2x token budget, send partial completion + hint to client; prefer early-stop over blocking UI. Explore Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching when many background analyses run.
- Model/versioning: prefer pinning to stable-2.1-small for mainline completions; want automatic fallback to quantized variants (smaller/lower-cost) when Dedicated capacity constrained. Canary rollouts important for dev channel.
- Security: VPC + SSO mandatory for enterprise customers. KMS integration for model key wrapping. Audit logs retention 1 year.
- Cost sensitivity: POC sees ~40% cost increase vs naive batching but 3x engagement lift in internal beta — product wants to tune token budgets to hit cost/engagement SLOs.
- Quote from PM: "We care more about consistent feel than raw throughput. If streaming jitter spikes, users report it as a bug."
- Next docs shared: pricing deck (drive), streaming integration guide (drive), security FAQ (drive).
